text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- President Hosni Mubarak appointed 10 new provincial governors and moved four to other provinces. He will meet the governors today after they take the oath of office.

- Manpower and Employment Minister Ahmed el-Amawi said his ministry would keep in contact with the U.N. compensation committee in Geneva on the transfer of 480 million pounds ($140 million) -- the second tranche of compensation for Egyptians who left the Gulf after the Iraqi invasion of Kuwait.
- Supply and Trade Minister Ahmed Gueily, after talks in Washington, said Congress would approve aid to Egypt in 1998 without any problems.

- Mubarak issued a decree appointing staff Major-General Mahmoud Mohamed Khalaf as commander of the Presidential Guard. General Khalaf graduated from staff college in 1964 and has served as chief of staff of the Third Army and as an aide-de-camp at the Presidency.
- Tourism Minister Mamdouh el-Beltagi told Prime Minister Kamal Ganzouri that 1.9 million tourists have visited Egypt in six months.
- Foreign Minister Amr Moussa will deliver messages to Presidents Zine al-Abidine Ben Ali of Tunisia and Liamine Zeroual of Algeria during a North African tour.

- The authorities have recently destroyed 519 tonnes of meat imported from France because it was not fit for consumption. This shows there are tight controls on meat imports, an Interior Ministry official said.
